owners.note: Five separate copies inside the JMX MBean, bypassing SamplerPolicyUpdate entirely.

findings: JmxRuntimePolicyApplier.apply returns void (extension line 54). RuntimePolicyControlHandler reports SUCCESS after the applier returns, so the protocol result is decided without knowing whether the underlying CAS succeeded. Failure surfaces only as an MBean counter increment and a log line.

Multiple concurrent entry points converge on the same SamplerStateHolder instance, and each of the five per-field MBean setters performs an independent CAS. This is the multi-writer situation expected-base semantics exist to arbitrate.
JmxRuntimePolicyApplier does not route scrubbing fields; there is no PlatformScrubbingControl call in that class.
ReadAppliedStateHandler.read() exposes _meta.samplingConfigVersion and _meta.validationConfigVersion as separate values and does not read scrubbing state at all.

correctiveEvidence.verificationMethod: every entry below was read from src/main/java at the cited line; no caller was assumed. Claimed callers that do not exist are recorded with a NOT_* role rather than omitted.
correctiveEvidence.b1Finding: Three of the eight Category A leaves — exporter.enabled, propagation.trace-control-headers.enabled and diagnostics.log-level — are not held by any versioned holder. They are bare atomics with no version, no snapshot and no expected base, and two of the three are process-wide static singletons. The original S-01 inventory covered only the three VersionedStateHolder-backed holders, so it understated the accepted-state migration by three owners and overstated it by one (scrubbing, which is Category B).

crossOwnerFindings: Three of the eight Category A leaves have no version, no snapshot and no expected base today, so for them the accepted-state store adds ordering semantics that do not currently exist in any form.

Two of the three newly inventoried owners are process-wide static singletons (PlatformPropagationGate.SHARED, PlatformLogControl.SHARED). They are the closest thing the repository has to the second-owner risk that E3 invariant 15 forbids, and the accepted-state store removes both.

Only one write path of the three owners is gated: the Spring Actuator write, by platform.tracing.actuator.mutation-enabled (default false). Every agent-side domain MBean write is ungated, and RuntimeConfigApplier checks only MBean availability.
RuntimeControlMutationPolicy applies only to the unified protocol handler, and the unified protocol reaches none of these three owners. The gate and the reachable owners are disjoint sets.

export.enabled and propagation.enabled are accepted by TracingControlProtocolSchema and counted as valid mutation keys by RuntimePolicyControlDomainValidator, but JmxRuntimePolicyApplier ignores them, so a payload containing only those keys is reported SUCCESS while changing nothing. diagnostics.log-level has no wire key at all.

Spring can write propagation.trace-control-headers.enabled and diagnostics.log-level but cannot read either back: PlatformTracingJmxClient exposes no getter, and TracingActuatorEndpoint's read model omits both. exporter.enabled is observable only as a metric inside SpanExporterMetrics.EXPORT_ENABLED.

TracingActuatorEndpoint additionally mirrors exportEnabled into properties.getExporter().setEnabled(...) at line 256, creating a second mutable representation of one Category A leaf inside the Spring context.
